judged_text: The webhook persists JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, ...)) into credential.key with no validation against the target app's credential schema, even though every OAuth callback path in this codebase zod-validates token payloads before storing them. A parent pushing a malformed or truncated payload (wrong app's keys, missing expiry_date or refresh_token) creates a credential row that passes storage and then throws inside the app's CalendarService/VideoApiAdapter at first use, failing that user's bookings with parse errors that give no hint the bad data arrived via the sync webhook — the operator's only recovery path is re-running the parent push blind.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), the decrypted payload is accepted as arbitrary JSON (`const keys = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))`) and written directly to `prisma.credential.update/create` as `key: keys` with no validation against any app-specific credential schema (only `appStoreMetadata` is checked for slug/type). This makes it possible for a well-authenticated caller (secret header + encryption key) to persist malformed/truncated/wrong-shape credential data that will only be rejected later when CalendarService/VideoApiAdapter code attempts zod parsing on first use, causing runtime failures. The diff shows many OAuth flows continue to zod-validate refreshed token structures before updating credentials, highlighting the inconsistency the finding describes.
